name: Lucius
fiction_note: Lucius is an original fictional elder with a Roman senatorial appearance and a questioning philosophical manner. He is not Plato, Socrates, a historical senator or an actor’s likeness.
future_note: Marcus offers reactive milestone guidance. Lucius joins through completed government development; Gaius through completed barracks development. Their explicit seasonal council and authored Zeus/Ares dilemmas are available now. Campaign memory recalls retained records across rulers and shows its sources; earlier conversations are not saved as history. A larger pantheon remains future story work.

intro.title: A seat beside your council
intro.body: A civic seat gives public affairs a place to be heard. I am Lucius. I have seen an orderly square conceal an anxious city, and a comfortable treasury conceal an exhausted people. Let us ask what your figures actually tell us.
intro.counsel: Before choosing a remedy, name the cause. Then ask who will bear the cost.

lesson_counsel: Order imposed and trust earned may look alike for a season. Examine the factors before deciding which you have.
What fills the treasury must come from somewhere. Ask what remains with the people who sustain it.
An uncertain report deserves an honest question, not a confident invention.
A building serves the city only through what it actually does. Read its effects before trusting its name.

lessons.title: Name the causes of discontent
lessons.body: Inspect your settlement’s public order factors. Taxes, garrisons and civic conditions can pull in different directions. Read the selected city with me to see the same reported factors, then use the settlement’s own controls if you choose to change policy.

lessons.title: Count both the revenue and the burden
lessons.body: Income, growth and public order are separate readings. A tax decision should be weighed against all three. Your city panel supplies the actual controls and costs; I cannot predict a new policy’s exact outcome from a current snapshot.

lessons.title: Ask how much you can know
lessons.body: Societal reports may be exact, older surveys or limited rumours. Legitimacy and grievance are not interchangeable with public order. A missing figure is unknown. Use the date and reporting level before treating any reading as a present fact.

lessons.title: Give civic work a purpose
lessons.body: Compare each building’s displayed prerequisites, cost and effects with the needs you have identified. My seat in your council grants no funds, bonuses or authority. Show me opens the capital’s existing construction panel and purchases nothing.
